fields.h1: Build a Cleaning Service Landing Page for Booking Requests
fields.hero_description: Build a cleaning service landing page that takes booking requests and saves each one to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Goes Into a Page That Books Cleans
fields.features_subheading: A cleaning service landing page asks for what a booking needs and sends it to the scheduler. Emergent builds each part by prompt.
fields.feature_1:
The type of clean, as the first tap

Start the form with fixed choices such as Standard clean, Deep clean, Move-out, and Office. That first answer decides which questions follow and who sees the request.
fields.feature_2:
How often, asked before the address

Ask whether the visitor wants a recurring plan or a one-time clean. A recurring answer opens a question about the visit day; a one-time answer goes straight to the date.
fields.feature_3:
A date field that sets the urgency

Put the preferred date near the top of the form. The app compares it with today, and a request for this week reaches the crew lead ahead of the requests for next month.
fields.feature_4:
Requests kept in a database you own

Each request is saved as a row with the type of clean, the date, the size, and the contact details. The office marks the row Scheduled once the clean is on the calendar.
fields.feature_5:
An alert for the person who books it

Send recurring plans to the scheduler by email and urgent move-outs to a crew lead in Slack. Each alert carries the visitor's name and phone number for a quick callback.
fields.feature_6:
Full code when you want it

On paid plans, Emergent exports the page's full code to your GitHub repository. Until a developer needs it, you change the page by describing the change you want in a prompt.

fields.tab_content_1:
Every recurring request lands on Mairead's list

Larkspen Home Cleaning opens its form on one choice: Recurring plan or One-time clean. A Recurring plan request goes to Mairead Birchall, who sets the visit day and the crew. A One-time clean gets a quote from the office. This month 40 requests came in: 26 were recurring and 14 were one-time.
fields.tab_content_2:
With 3 days or less left, Anneke gets the request

Elmbranch Move-Out Cleaning asks for the move-out date before the address. A date 3 days or less away emails Anneke Visser, the crew lead for short-notice jobs. Any later date goes on next week's schedule. This week 12 move-out requests came in: 4 were short notice and 8 were later.
fields.tab_content_3:
For 5,000 sq ft or more, a walkthrough comes first

Gablewood Office Cleaning visits large offices before it quotes. The form asks for the office size, and 5,000 sq ft or more books a walkthrough with Rowena Petrassi, the account manager. A smaller office gets its price by email. This quarter 18 offices asked: 7 booked a walkthrough and 11 got a price.
fields.tab_content_4:
The oven and the fridge are priced on the page

Hollowbrook Cleaning Co. lists its extras with a price next to each: $35 for inside the oven and $30 for inside the fridge, on top of a $220 deep clean. The total updates with each tick: a request with both shows $285. This week 22 deep clean requests came in: 14 added an extra and 8 did not.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Cleaning Service Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Follow these 7 steps to build a cleaning service landing page that sends each booking request to the person who schedules it.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the one request the page is for
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask how often before you ask who
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Put the service date near the top
fields.howto_step_1_des: Give a deep clean ad its own page and a recurring plan offer another. A visitor who clicked for a move-out clean needs a date field, not a plan price, and one button keeps the page on one request.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open with the frequency question, then ask for the name and phone number. A recurring visitor is worth a call from the scheduler, and that first answer tells the app where to send the request.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for the preferred date with a date picker instead of a text box. A typed "next Friday" cannot be sorted, while a picked date lets a short-notice job reach the crew lead first.
fields.howto_step_4_des: List add-ons such as inside the oven or interior windows as checkboxes, each with its price. Leave off any extra you only quote after seeing the home, and offer a notes box for anything unusual.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Decide who hears about each request
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write one routing line per case in your prompt, such as move-outs this week to the crew lead and every other request to the office inbox. Emergent builds the routing from those lines and changes it when you prompt again.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Show a price where the job allows it
fields.howto_step_6_des: Put a fixed price on the page for cleans you sell by the visit, such as a standard clean by bedroom count. Keep large offices as quote requests, and say on the page that the price follows a visit.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit the form once per route with your own phone number. Confirm that the row shows the right type of clean in the database, and that the email or Slack alert reaches the person it names.

faq_plan.q: What is a cleaning service landing page?
faq_plan.a: A cleaning service landing page is one page built to get a booking request for a specific clean, such as a recurring home clean or a move-out. It asks what clean the visitor needs, when, and how to reach them, and it leaves out the menus a full website carries.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a cleaning service landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe the page to Emergent's AI landing page builder, listing each clean you offer and the person who schedules it. Emergent builds the page and the database behind it from that prompt. Send a test request, adjust anything by prompting again, and publish when it works. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What is the first question to ask on a cleaning service landing page?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the type of clean first, as one tap on a short list such as Standard, Deep, Move-out, and Office. That answer decides which questions follow: a homeowner never sees office questions. Ask for the date and phone number next, and leave the address until the clean is picked.

faq_plan.q: Where should the request form sit on a cleaning service landing page?
faq_plan.a: Put it at the top, where it shows on the first screen of a phone. Keep the headline and the form together, then add photos of finished rooms below for visitors who scroll before they book. The same short shape suits a pest control landing page, where the request form also does the selling.

faq_plan.q: Does move-out cleaning need its own cleaning service landing page?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if you run ads for it. A move-out visitor cares about one date and an empty home, while a recurring visitor cares about a visit day and the same crew each time. A separate page can ask for the move-out date first and route short-notice jobs to whoever takes them.

faq_plan.q: How can a cleaning service landing page win recurring customers?
faq_plan.a: It can offer the recurring plan as the first choice on the form, with the visit frequency next to it. After a one-time clean, send the customer a link back to that page with the plan already picked. Keep the request rows: the office can then see who booked once and has not come back.

faq_plan.q: Can one cleaning service landing page cover home and office cleaning?
faq_plan.a: It can, but a page for each lets every visitor answer only the questions that fit them. An office manager wants a walkthrough and an invoice, while a homeowner wants a date and a price. A contractor landing page faces the same split between homeowners and commercial jobs.

faq_plan.q: How should a cleaning service landing page handle add-ons like oven cleaning?
faq_plan.a: List each add-on as a checkbox with its price, and update the total as the visitor ticks them. Save the ticked add-ons on the request row, where the crew can see what to bring. If an extra needs a look first, such as carpet stains, mark it as quoted on the visit.

faq_plan.q: What should a cleaning service landing page do after a visitor books?
faq_plan.a: It should show the visitor a confirmation that says when to expect a call, and the person who books the clean should get an alert with the details. Emergent builds both from the prompt, along with Slack, email, or in-app alerts. Each booking is saved in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How do I track which ads send visitors to my cleaning service landing page?
faq_plan.a: Point each ad at its own page, or ask Emergent to add a hidden field that records which ad the visitor came from. Each request row then carries its source, and the office can count booked cleans per ad. The same split by ad works on any hvac landing page that runs separate repair and tune-up ads.

plan.angle: The cleaning service landing page SERP has no Semrush top 10 (Wave 3, not SERP-checked) and no gate-passing AlsoAsked questions, so the page wins on substance a gallery cannot give: four cleaning service landing pages built around the booking request itself (a recurring-or-one-time split, a move-out date that decides urgency, an office size that decides walkthrough or emailed quote, deep clean add-ons priced on the page), each with the form, the routing and the database row behind it, then the build steps. It makes no claims about insurance, bonding, licensing, chemicals or anything state-specific. HVAC, plumber, contractor and pest control pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.

findings.quote: Build a cleaning service landing page that saves every signup to a database I own.
findings.issue: A cleaning service page takes booking requests, not signups; the hero ("takes booking requests"), features ("Each request is saved as a row") and every tab use request/booking, so the prompt box breaks the same-term-for-the-same-thing rule. The field is code-built (skeleton default), so the fix belongs in the generator, not a hand edit.
findings.fix: Have the skeleton pick the hub noun per page type, e.g. "Build a cleaning service landing page that saves every booking request to a database I own."; flag the code default to the coordinator for service-business pages.

findings.quote: Ask for the type of clean first, as one tap on a short list such as Standard, Deep, Move-out, and Office.
findings.issue: FAQ answers restate body sections with words swapped: FAQ 3 restates feature_1 ("Start the form with fixed choices such as Standard clean, Deep clean, Move-out, and Office"); FAQ 8 "List each add-on as a checkbox with its price" restates howto_step_4_des "List add-ons such as inside the oven or interior windows as checkboxes, each with its price" and its quote-on-visit line; FAQ 9 "Each booking is saved in a database you own." restates why_description "with every request in a database you own" and feature_4.
findings.fix: Next pass: let FAQ 3 and 8 add something the body does not (what to do when a visitor picks two types; how the crew sees the extras on the row) instead of repeating it.

findings.quote: See how four cleaning companies route recurring, move-out, office and deep clean requests
findings.issue: Three tabs route requests to a person, but the deep clean tab (Hollowbrook) prices extras on the page and routes nothing; the verb "route" stretches over the fourth example. Also no serial comma before "and deep clean" while the body uses serial commas ("Standard clean, Deep clean, Move-out, and Office").
findings.fix: "See how four cleaning companies handle recurring, move-out, office, and deep clean requests, then build your cleaning service landing page." (check length)

findings.issue: QC Q9 flags "clean" 21x, "request" 15x and "recurring" 13x outside the FAQ; the nouns are the buyer's literal vocabulary, so this reads as precise rather than padded, but the density is high in tab_content_1 ("Recurring plan" x2, "recurring" x1 in four sentences).
findings.fix: Accepted as the trade's vocabulary; vary where a pronoun or "visit" reads as naturally.
